description: DIFMS (Digital Indian Farming & Monitoring System) is our college team project for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We combine NASA Earth observation and satellite data with weather, soil, IoT, and market information to support farmers. For Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, DIFMS provides farm-specific recommendations for crop selection, climate adaptation, irrigation, and sustainable agriculture.
summary:
DIFMS (Digital Indian Farming and Monitoring System), developed by Team VARAHI AGRI, is an AI-powered smart agriculture platform that integrates NASA satellite data, IoT ground stations, and Artificial Intelligence to support Indian farmers in making informed farming decisions.

Our system considers different agricultural land types, including black soil, red soil, alluvial soil, drylands, rainfed lands, irrigated lands, and coastal agricultural lands. Based on these land characteristics, we propose installing representative IoT ground stations to collect real-time information such as soil moisture, soil temperature, humidity, and pH.

DIFMS combines this ground-level information with NASA POWER climate data, satellite observations, and agricultural market-demand information. Our AI system analyses these datasets to recommend suitable crops based on land conditions, weather, water availability, and market demand.

The platform also supports GPS-based land measurement, crop monitoring, smart irrigation, crop health analysis, and farmer-to-buyer connections.

Our vision is to transform traditional farming into data-driven, profitable, and sustainable agriculture through space technology and intelligent solutions.
details:
Digital Indian Farming and Monitoring System (DIFMS)

1. What Does DIFMS Do?

DIFMS (Digital Indian Farming and Monitoring System), developed by Team VARAHI AGRI, is an integrated smart agriculture platform designed to transform traditional farming into data-driven and sustainable agriculture. It connects NASA satellite data, IoT ground stations, Artificial Intelligence, GPS technology, and agricultural market information to support farmers from land preparation and crop selection to harvesting, insurance support, and marketing.

2. How Does It Work?

A. Land-Type-Based Monitoring System

India has different agricultural land and soil types, including black soil, red soil, alluvial soil, drylands, rainfed lands, irrigated lands, and coastal agricultural lands.

DIFMS considers these differences when planning representative IoT ground stations in agricultural regions to monitor local soil and environmental conditions.

B. IoT Ground-Level Data Collection

The proposed IoT ground stations collect:

  • Soil moisture
  • Soil temperature
  • Soil pH
  • Air temperature
  • Humidity

These measurements help understand actual agricultural field conditions.

C. NASA Satellite and Climate Data Integration

DIFMS uses NASA POWER API and NASA Earth observation resources to obtain climate and environmental information, including rainfall, temperature, solar radiation, and other relevant parameters.

Combining satellite observations with ground-level measurements provides a better understanding of agricultural conditions.

D. AI-Based Demand-Driven Crop Selection

Our AI system analyses land characteristics, soil conditions, NASA climate information, ground-level IoT measurements, water availability, and agricultural market demand.

Based on these factors, DIFMS recommends suitable crops for particular agricultural regions while considering market opportunities.

Our objective is to help farmers identify the right crop for the right land at the right time.

E. GPS-Based Land Measurement

Farmers can identify and measure their agricultural land using GPS-based polygon mapping technology. This helps calculate cultivation areas and maintain digital farm information.

F. AI-Based Crop Monitoring and Disease Detection

Farmers can upload photographs of their crops periodically to monitor crop growth.

If crops show signs of disease or damage, farmers can upload photographs. Our AI-assisted image analysis system identifies possible visible symptoms and provides suggestions for disease management, preventive measures, and appropriate agricultural practices.

This helps farmers identify potential crop health problems and take timely action.

G. Smart Irrigation and Water Management

IoT soil moisture sensors help farmers monitor water requirements. The system supports remote motor control and smart irrigation using connected hardware, helping reduce unnecessary water consumption and improve water management.

H. Government Agricultural Scheme Monitoring

DIFMS aims to support transparent monitoring of government agricultural schemes through GPS-based land identification, satellite observations, periodic crop photographs, and digital farm records.

Government departments can use this information to verify agricultural activities, monitor the progress of supported farming activities, and identify discrepancies between reported and observed field conditions.

This can help reduce duplicate reporting, unnecessary expenditure, and wastage of public funds while improving accountability and effective utilization of government scheme resources.

I. Smart Crop Insurance and Damage Assessment

DIFMS aims to support agricultural crop insurance processes by integrating GPS-based farm boundaries, NASA weather information, satellite observations, ground-level IoT data, and farmer-uploaded crop photographs.

In cases of floods, droughts, excessive rainfall, or other crop-damaging conditions, the system can help document affected agricultural areas and provide supporting information for crop-loss assessment.

This information can assist farmers, insurance providers, and government departments in verification and insurance claim documentation. Final insurance eligibility and claim settlement remain subject to the applicable insurance scheme rules and authorized assessment.

J. Farmer-to-Buyer Connection

DIFMS provides a platform to connect farmers with buyers. Information about crop availability and market demand can help farmers identify potential buyers and improve marketing opportunities.

3. Technologies and Tools Used

NASA and Space-Based Resources

  • NASA POWER API – Climate and environmental data.
  • NASA Earth observation resources – Satellite-based agricultural and environmental information.

Artificial Intelligence

  • Google Gemini AI – AI-assisted data analysis, crop recommendations, and image-based crop health suggestions.

Software and Development Tools

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript – Web application development.
  • Google Apps Script – Application backend and integration.
  • Google Sheets – Data storage and management.
  • Google Cloud – Cloud-based development and services.

IoT and Hardware

  • ESP32 / ESP8266 microcontrollers.
  • Soil moisture sensors.
  • Temperature and humidity sensors.
  • Soil pH sensors.
  • Relay modules and motor-control systems.
  • GPS technology for land measurement.

4. What Makes DIFMS Creative and Innovative?

The main innovation of DIFMS is integrating space-based information with actual ground-level agricultural measurements, AI intelligence, and market-demand information in one digital platform.

Instead of recommending the same crop to every farmer, DIFMS considers different agricultural land types and local environmental conditions.

It also extends beyond crop selection by integrating:

  • Land-type-based IoT monitoring.
  • Demand-driven crop recommendations.
  • AI-assisted crop disease identification.
  • Smart irrigation and water management.
  • Government agricultural scheme monitoring.
  • Crop insurance documentation and damage assessment.
  • Farmer-to-buyer connections.

This creates an integrated digital agricultural ecosystem rather than a standalone crop recommendation application.

5. Factors Considered by Our Team

  1. Different agricultural soil and land types.
  2. Rainfall and changing climatic conditions.
  3. Soil moisture and water availability.
  4. Soil pH and temperature.
  5. Crop suitability and growing conditions.
  6. Local and regional market demand.
  7. Crop diseases and agricultural risks.
  8. Government scheme transparency and accountability.
  9. Crop insurance and natural disaster impacts.
  10. Water conservation and sustainable agriculture.
  11. Affordability and accessibility of technology for Indian farmers.
  12. Scalability across different agricultural regions.

6. Benefits and Intended Impact

DIFMS aims to deliver the following benefits:

  • Help farmers make informed crop-selection decisions.
  • Reduce crop-selection risks through data-based recommendations.
  • Identify possible crop diseases earlier through AI-assisted image analysis.
  • Improve water management and irrigation efficiency.
  • Support transparent monitoring of government agricultural schemes.
  • Reduce unnecessary expenditure and wastage of public funds.
  • Support crop damage documentation and insurance assessment.
  • Connect farmers with potential buyers.
  • Improve agricultural resource utilization.
  • Encourage climate-resilient and sustainable farming.

7. Our Vision

Our vision is to bring space technology from satellites to the soil and make advanced agricultural intelligence accessible to every farmer.

From Land Identification to Seed Selection, Crop Monitoring, Disease Detection, Irrigation, Insurance Support, Government Scheme Monitoring, and Crop Marketing – Everything in One Digital Platform.

DIFMS: Smart Farming, Better Profits, Transparent Governance, and a Sustainable Future for Indian Agriculture.

Developed by Team VARAHI AGRI.
